sources: The CAT candidate portal (iimcat.ac.in) and the process followed in recent CAT cycles

admitCard.where: Your CAT candidate login on iimcat.ac.in
admitCard.when: Admit cards are made available a few weeks before the exam, usually in the last week of October or early November (check the official schedule for the date)
steps: Open iimcat.ac.in and sign in with your CAT user ID and password.
Open the admit card link when it goes live and download it.
Check your slot, reporting time, test centre address and photo on it.
Print it and keep it with you, with the ID proof the instructions name.
carry: The original photo ID named in the instructions
Only what the instructions allow. Rough sheets and the on-screen calculator are provided at the centre, as the instructions describe
admitCard.note: CAT is held in more than one slot on the same day. Your slot is printed on the admit card.

answerKey.summary: After the exam, the CAT portal releases your response sheet and the provisional answer key, with a short window to challenge answers.
steps: Sign in to iimcat.ac.in with your user ID and password.
Open the response sheet and answer key section, and download the response sheet for your slot.
Compare your responses with the provisional key.
To challenge an answer, select the question, give your reason and pay the fee before the window closes.
answerKey.fee: A fee is charged for each question challenged. The amount is fixed in that year's notice, so check it before you pay.
answerKey.note: CAT scores are scaled across the three slots and reported as percentiles, so your raw score cannot be converted to a percentile exactly from the response sheet.

result.summary: The CAT result is published on iimcat.ac.in with a scorecard for each candidate, usually in January.

stages.what: Section-wise scaled scores and percentiles, plus the overall score and percentile.
Each institute shortlists on its own criteria and calls candidates for written ability and personal interview rounds.
Final selection is made by each institute, using CAT percentile, academics, work experience and the interview.

result.scorecard: The scorecard is valid for the admission cycle of that year. Institutes access the scores through the CAT portal, so you do not send a copy.
